bihar_raw_news.title: ITC expands dairy play in East India, bets on branded milk - The Economic Times
bihar_raw_news.content: ETMarkets.com ITC is expanding its fresh dairy presence in Eastern India through Aashirvaad, betting on rising demand for branded milk and value-added dairy products across Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand. ITC is solidifying its position in Eastern India's fresh dairy market through its flagship Aashirvaad brand , leveraging growing consumer appetite for branded milk and value-added offerings across Bihar, West Bengal, and Jharkhand. Since entering the fresh dairy segment in 2018 with the rollout of Aashirvaad milk in Bihar—followed by expansions into West Bengal and Jharkhand—the diversified conglomerate has established itself as the second-largest dairy brand in Bihar. Its product suite spans fresh milk, curd, paneer, lassi, and Mishti Doi. To drive its market expansion, ITC has tailored its dairy portfolio to align with regional palates, local consumption habits, and rising demand for reliable, quality-certified dairy products. Also read: Soap & shampoo veg or non-veg? A dot on the pack will now tell you Addressing potential geographical expansion, Hemant Malik, Chief Executive Officer, Foods Division, and Executive Director, ITC, emphasized that Eastern India remains the central focus for the company's dairy roadmap due to substantial untapped potential. Live Events "East is one of the most promising growth markets for the dairy category and will be central to our growth strategy in the coming years," Malik told PTI. Malik highlighted that in Bihar, over 80 percent of consumers still buy loose milk, creating a "compelling opportunity" to convert households toward packaged, value-added dairy options that guarantee quality, safety, and uniformity. "In South India, consumers moved to branded curd over a decade ago, and we wanted to enable a similar transition in Bihar. With our pouch curd offerings, we are helping consumers shift to branded curd that delivers assured quality and consistency, backed by the trust of ITC," said Malik. Looking ahead in the value-added segment, ITC is assessing novel and healthier dessert formats to diversify its offerings beyond established products like Mishti Doi. For ITC, dairy stands out as "one of the fastest-growing categories witnessing high double-digit growth". The company currently manages dairy processing plants across several regional hubs: Munger, Patna, Muzaffarpur, and Gaya in Bihar; Ranchi in Jharkhand; and Howrah and Bardhaman in West Bengal. Through its Project Gomukh initiative, ITC engages with over 40,000 dairy farmers via direct milk sourcing networks. Also read: Protein boom sparks deals, partnerships across F&B space "The overarching objective of the project is to increase milk productivity and improve the quality of milk, while empowering rural farmers and increasing their income," the company stated. Aiming to secure leadership in India's FMCG landscape, ITC has grown the Aashirvaad umbrella beyond atta into staples, spices, fresh foods, and frozen products, targeting a doubling of consumer spends to exceed Rs 20,000 crore over the next five years. According to the company's latest annual report, the 'Aashirvaad Svasti' fresh dairy business sustained robust momentum through FY26, driven by gains in its premium 'Select' milk variant and strong sales in value-added lines including curd, paneer, Mishti Doi, and lassi.

bihar_raw_news.title: "Opposition's allegations regarding SIR are baseless and factless": Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: "Opposition's allegations regarding SIR are baseless and factless": Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Sep 27, 2026 19:32 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 27 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday dismissed the questions raised by various political parties against the Election Commission of India as "baseless". The Chief Minister asserted that the "SIR process in Bihar was completed following prescribed rules and in a transparent manner, ensuring that no eligible person's name was removed from the electoral rolls while full provisions for claims and objections remained available." Detailing the timeline, CM Choudhary stated that the SIR process in Bihar was conducted from June 24, 2025, to July 25, 2025, during which entries related to deceased persons, permanently relocated individuals, and voters registered at multiple locations were verified. He noted that a similar SIR was conducted in 2003 when Rabri Devi was Chief Minister, and again in 2025 under Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Accusing the opposition of spreading confusion at a press conference, he said, "Opposition leaders have no facts; they are only making allegations." He added that the Election Commission had made the 2003 voter list available online so eligible voters could cross-verify their legacy details. Addressing questions raised by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and RJD leader Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, the Chief Minister said the Election Commission had already clarified the matters. He emphasised that Aadhaar cards were accepted as identity proof following Supreme Court directives, though the apex court has clarified that Aadhaar establishes identity but is not proof of citizenship. He maintained that no genuine complaints regarding the exclusion of eligible voters have been received so far, while noting that proper channels under established procedures remain open for any valid grievances. Reiterating respect for democratic institutions, the Chief Minister said the opposition has every right to present its views in a democratic setup, but urged them to do so with facts and evidence. He stressed that both the Election Commission and the judiciary are vital pillars of democracy, and electoral complaints can be addressed through these proper institutions. Hitting out at the opposition over broader political issues, CM Choudhary said the pace of national development has accelerated under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "A poor man's son became the Prime Minister of the country, and the opposition cannot digest this. The country is running well, and the opposition dislikes this. They have no issues left, which is why they are engaged in spreading confusion," he remarked. Highlighting welfare initiatives such as housing schemes for the poor and marginalised, the Chief Minister stated that the public is the ultimate master in a democracy and chooses its representatives through the ballot. He urged all political parties to go among the public with issues of public interest and present their case factually. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's ₹21000 crore mineral reserves may generate over ₹5000 crore annual revenue, says report
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar’s ₹21,000 crore mineral reserves may generate over ₹5,000 crore annual revenue, says report Bihar aims to revitalise its mineral economy by harnessing new resources worth over ₹ 21,000 crore. Geological surveys have reportedly identified valuable minerals like glauconite and gold, but challenges remain in transitioning to commercial production. Garvit Bhirani Updated 27 Sep 2026, 05:23 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Bihar discovers ₹21,000 cr mineral wealth, eyes ₹5,000 cr annual revenue: Report (AI-generated image for representational purposes only) AI Quick Read Bihar is reportedly seeking to rebuild its mineral economy after decades of being left with little of the mineral wealth that remained with Jharkhand following the states’ bifurcation in 2000. Geological investigations conducted between 2021 and 2024 have identified mineral resources estimated at more than ₹ 21,000 crore across Rohtas, Jamui, Gaya and Jehanabad, reported The Indian Express. The discoveries could potentially generate more than ₹ 5,000 crore in annual mining revenue once the identified resources are converted into operational mines, according to state officials. That would be significantly higher than Bihar’s current record mining collection of ₹ 3,592 crore, which comes predominantly from minor minerals such as sand and stone. However, the transition from geological discoveries to commercial production remains a major challenge. The state is targeting mineral extraction across different projects between 2026 and 2031, with exploration, auctions, clearances and mining leases still to be completed. What minerals has Bihar discovered? Rohtas accounts for a major share of the identified resources. Geological surveys have found around 130.11 million tonnes of glauconite across the Pipradih-Bhurwa and Chutia-Nauhatta blocks, with an estimated value of ₹ 14,048 crore. Glauconite can serve as a source of potassium for fertilisers , a potentially significant resource for India given its dependence on imports for potash fertilisers. Also Read | Nepal floods: A Bihar village grapples with loss and debt The Bhora-Kathra block in Rohtas has also been identified with 33-39.68 million tonnes of high-grade limestone, valued at about ₹ 1,761.42 crore. The mineral is widely used in cement manufacturing and for producing quicklime. Rohtas is also home to the Amjhor pyrite deposits, which account for nearly 95% of India's known pyrite resources. Pyrites are used in sulfuric acid production and other industrial chemical processes. Jamui’s magnetite and gold potential Jamui has emerged as another important mineral zone, particularly for magnetite and gold. The Majos block contains an estimated 48.40 million tonnes of magnetite, with an assessed value ranging from ₹ 3,817.60 crore to ₹ 6,000 crore. The Bhanta block has another 6.49 million tonnes, valued at around ₹ 511.91 crore. Magnetite is primarily used as iron ore in steelmaking and other metallurgical applications. Exploration has identified 222.88 million tonnes of ore containing an estimated 37.6 tonnes of gold metal. The Sono resource is classified as a remaining resource rather than a reserve. bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Opposition raising false alarm over SIR name deletions, says Bihar CM India Opposition raising false alarm over SIR name deletions, says Bihar CM PTI 27 September, 2026 03:47 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 27 (PTI) Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday accused opposition parties of raising a false alarm over deletion of voters from Bihar’s electoral list in the SIR conducted ahead of the 2025 assembly elections. Terming Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi the “prince” of Congress, the senior BJP leader said that he toured Bihar ahead of last year’s assembly polls and raised allegations that several voter names were struck off the electoral list illegally. “But no case of illegal deletion could be proved,” Choudhary told a press conference here. He alleged that the opposition parties were raising a “false alarm” over the issue. Show Full Article “During the SIR in Bihar, 22.34 lakh voters were found dead, 36.28 lakh voters moved from one place to another, and seven lakh voters were registered at two places. These names were deleted, but no counter-claims or applications were received,” he said. The Election Commission has been under fire following a news report of disquiet within the poll panel over pan-India SIR. Seeking to capitalise on the opportunity, opposition parties have demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with Gandhi alleging that the poll panel chief was made in charge of “match-fixing” India’s elections by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls that they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The objections covered changes to the statutory voter registration Form 6, the handling of additions and deletions from electoral rolls, and centralised control over the electoral roll database. However, the poll panel asserted that all SIR orders received unanimous consent from all three commissioners and that updates to Form 6 for voter enrolment were upheld by the Supreme Court. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar prepares for 2030 FIH women's hockey world cup in Rajgir - The Bridge
bihar_raw_news.content: Begin typing your search above and press return to search. Home Hockey Hockey Bihar prepares for 2030 FIH women's hockey world cup in Rajgir Sports Minister Shreyasi Singh says Bihar's hosting proposal has been accepted, building on Rajgir's record of staging international hockey tournaments. X Rajgir has hosted two major international hockey tournaments in recent years, helping establish the city as a venue for continental competition. (Photo credit: The Bihar Index/X) By The Bridge Desk Published: 27 Sept 2026 3:13 PM IST Bihar has stepped up preparations to host the 2030 FIH Women's Hockey World Cup in Rajgir, with Sports Minister Shreyasi Singh stating that the state government's proposal for the tournament has been accepted. The proposal was discussed during the 2026 Asian Games in Japan. Singh, Bihar Sports Department Secretary Deepak Anand and Hockey India Secretary General Bhola Singh were present during the discussions. According to Patna Press, the state sees the proposed tournament as an opportunity to strengthen Bihar's presence in international sport and provide greater exposure to its emerging women hockey players. Singh said the arrival of leading women hockey players from around the world would allow young athletes in Bihar to watch international-level competition closely and draw inspiration from the players. She added that hosting the tournament could help create a stronger environment for promoting women's hockey and identifying emerging talent across the state. “Our dream is that the world's daughters come to Bihar and Bihar's daughters reach the world,” Singh said, outlining the state's ambition to connect local athletes with the international sporting community. Rajgir's international hockey record Rajgir has hosted two major international hockey tournaments in recent years, helping establish the city as a venue for continental competition. The city hosted the Women's Asian Champions Trophy from November 11 to 20, 2024. The tournament featured India, China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand. India defeated China 1-0 in the final to claim the title. Rajgir subsequently hosted the Men's Asia Cup from August 29 to September 7, 2025. India won the tournament, adding to the city's record of hosting international hockey competitions. These events have increased the visibility of Bihar's sporting infrastructure and provided experience in staging competitions involving international teams. Focus on grassroots development The proposed 2030 World Cup is being positioned by the state as an opportunity to promote women's hockey and inspire young players. Singh said exposure to the world's leading athletes could help young hockey players set new goals and aspire to compete at international level. The tournament would also bring international attention to Rajgir and Bihar's sports facilities. However, the final hosting arrangements and formal confirmation of the tournament's venue by the International Hockey Federation have not been detailed in the report. Bihar's latest initiative builds on its recent hosting experience, with the state seeking to connect international sporting events with grassroots participation and the development of women athletes. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary calls for compulsory computer education in all govt schools
bihar_raw_news.content: Government Policies 1 min read Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary calls for compulsory computer education in all govt schools Choudhary asks education officials to prepare a plan from next year, with one computer instructor proposed for every two to three schools; also calls for modern facilities and stronger academic support. Madan Kumar TOI.in Published On Sep 27, 2026 at 08:17 AM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook CM at Govt Middle School, Ramjichak, under Danapur in Patna district Patna: CM Samrat Choudhary has asked officials to equip govt schools with modern facilities and strengthen their academic environment to prepare students for competitive examinations. Choudhary issued the directions while attending a parent-teacher meeting at Govt Middle School, Ramjichak, under Danapur in Patna district. He reviewed teaching arrangements, attendance, examination results and facilities, and interacted with students, parents and teachers. He directed education department officials to prepare a plan from next year to make computer education compulsory in all govt schools. He suggested one instructor for every two to three schools. He said online teachers and live classes had been provided at model schools at around 700 locations across Bihar. Advt Education minister Mithilesh Tiwari and cooperative minister-cum-Danapur MLA Ram Kripal Yadav were present. Choudhary said regular parent-teacher meetings should improve education quality, ensure teacher availability and 100% attendance, besides identifying students needing additional support. He also reviewed the statewide ‘Seva Chitra’ competition under the ‘Mere Sapnon ka Bharat-Seva Chitra’ campaign and appreciated students’ work on themes including Viksit Bharat-2047, solar energy, metro trains, robots and Sapnon ka Bharat. bihar_raw_news.title: MP Govt releases Bhopal Master Plan 2047 draft | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 MP Govt releases Bhopal Master Plan 2047 draft Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Services The Madhya Pradesh Government has released the draft of the Bhopal Master Plan 2047, setting the stage for public consultation on the proposed land-use framework for the State Capital. The notification was issued on Saturday, days after the Supreme Court considered issues related to commercial activity in Bhopal’s residential areas. The release of the draft plan has raised expectations among traders and property owners facing sealing action, particularly those seeking a change in the designated land use of their properties. However, the Supreme Court’s September 22 order makes it clear that publishing the draft master plan will not, by itself, provide immediate relief from existing sealing orders. The court has permitted the Government to publish the draft plan and invite claims and objections from stakeholders. At the same time, the State Government has assured the court that it will not finalise the proposed master plan without the court’s permission. Consequently, any proposed change in land use contained in the draft cannot automatically make an existing commercial activity in a residential area lawful. The Supreme Court order, which was made public on Friday, deals with Bhopal in paragraphs 17 to 26. During the hearing, the State Government informed the court that the draft of the new master plan had been prepared and sought permission to place it in the public domain for objections and suggestions. The court’s directions mean that the legal status of a property will continue to be determined under the applicable existing master plan and building regulations until the new plan is formally approved. Therefore, a shop or commercial establishment operating in an area currently designated exclusively for residential use could continue to face enforcement action despite a proposal in the draft plan to alter its land-use classification. The order also states that the pendency of a dispute relating to ownership of a property, building or any other matter will not, by itself, prevent authorities from taking action. Where a property is being used contrary to the purpose for which it was allotted or in violation of the approved plan, the competent authorities can proceed in accordance with law. Similarly, construction undertaken without the required approvals can be subjected to sealing or demolition action as prescribed under the applicable legal framework. The court has, however, made a distinction in cases where the existing land-use classification does not clearly specify whether an area is residential or commercial. In such locations, the possibility of mixed use may be considered in accordance with the applicable provisions. Until the issue is resolved, the existing status will remain in place while administrative and documentation processes can continue. The order is particularly significant for traders who had been hoping that the new master plan would immediately resolve the issue of sealing of commercial establishments in residential neighbourhoods. The court’s directions indicate that such relief cannot flow merely from a proposal contained in the draft

bihar_raw_news.title: Meet the 20-year-old whose wastewater innovation earned UNDP recognition
bihar_raw_news.content: Edited By : Anand P Last Updated: 27 September 2026, 09:17 AM IST Share A 20-year-old entrepreneur who moved from Bihar's Madhubani to Mumbai has developed an affordable wastewater treatment system aimed at reducing industrial pollution. Representational Image | Photo: AFP New Delhi: Growing up in the slums of Mumbai after moving from Bihar's Madhubani in search of a better life, Piyush Jha witnessed how wastewater accumulating around homes exposed residents to diseases such as dengue, malaria and typhoid. The experience prompted him to explore a solution to the problem, eventually leading him to develop an affordable wastewater treatment technology that has now earned recognition from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). At just 20, Jha has developed a decentralised, modular wastewater treatment system designed to make wastewater treatment more accessible and affordable, particularly for industries. His innovation has been recognised through UNDP India's entrepreneurship initiative, the 'Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge'. Speaking to PTI on the occasion of World Rivers Day, Jha said his innovation seeks to tackle one of the major sources of pollution in India's water bodies: the discharge of untreated industrial wastewater. He estimated that nearly 18,000 million litres of wastewater are discharged daily in India, of which only 20 to 30 per cent is treated. "We don't require any chemical dosing to treat wastewater, nor do we require heavy civil infrastructure. The current water treatment plants require heavy civil infrastructure just to get started, which is a major concern for manufacturing and processing plants in India," he said. Jha said the technology could indirectly benefit the common person by offering industries a more affordable way to treat wastewater before it is released into the environment. The system is designed for industries such as textiles, leather, food and beverages, distilleries, paper and pulp, and sugar, which generate large volumes of biodegradable waste. The technology uses microorganisms to break down waste while generating electricity in the process, he said. "When small and medium-scale industries get an affordable water treatment solution, they're less likely to discharge toxic wastewater into water bodies. It also helps them financially. An industry may earlier spend Rs 20 lakh on operational costs for water treatment, which our pretreatment solution reduces to Rs 5 to 7 lakh," he told PTI. Industry partnerships and pilot opportunities Jha said his company has already started working with several industry partners interested in the technology. These include Mumbai-based cleantech startup Indra Water, which develops compact, decentralised wastewater treatment systems, and Pune-based sweets and snacks enterprise Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale. He has also received a conditional purchase order from Dahej Waste Service, a Bharuch-based company in Gujarat that provides commercial and industrial cleaning and waste management services. From a second-hand laptop to a startup Recalling how the idea took shape, Jha said his entrepreneurial journey began during the Covid-19 pandemic, when his mother helped him arrange a second-hand laptop. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that the surgical strike by the Indian Army on the terrorist hideouts in Pakistan demonstrated a new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy to the world. Addressing the nation in his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani, Mr Modi said India is set to mark the tenth anniversary of the surgical strike tomorrow (28th September). He said the world was astonished to see the manner in which brave Indian soldiers crossed the Line of Control to take action against terrorism. Prime Minister Modi said the surgical strike was India’s decisive response to the long-standing pain the nation had endured due to terrorist attacks. He stated that over the past decade – from the Balakot airstrike to ‘Operation Sindoor ’, India has repeatedly sent the message that terrorist strikes will be met with a befitting response. Mr Modi recounted that there was a time when serial blasts had become a common occurrence in the country. He said many lives were lost in the serial blasts in Delhi on 13th September, 2008. The 26/11 attack took place just a few weeks later in Mumbai. He highlighted that today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and country is witnessing the results of that. Prime Minister Modi said this year also marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks. He said that the highest number of victims at the World Trade Center in the US, after Americans, were Indians. He recalled paying homage to those innocent citizens during his US visit after becoming Prime Minister in 2014. He once again extended his condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of crores of Indian citizens. Touching upon the topic of the ongoing census, Mr Modi said the first phase of this exercise is nearly complete across all States and Union Territories. Data of over 32 crore families has already been recorded. Work is currently underway also in the remote, snow-clad regions of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand. The Prime Minister noted that many inspiring experiences have emerged from these areas. In Uttarakhand, the census process began in the village of Mana in Chamoli, which is known as the country’s first village. Prime Minister Modi said the process there started with 83-year-old Purnima Rawat. In Bagori village of Uttarkashi, Hardev Singh Rana, who runs a homestay, entered his details himself using digital means. Mr Modi emphasised that the census is a national responsibility for all. He added that the facility to self-register census details is very convenient and people can register information about themselves and their family from their mobiles. Along with Hindi, this facility is available in 16 languages. The Prime Minister asked people to visit the census online portal, se.census.gov.in, and log in with their mobile number, enter location, fill in details regarding their family and submit the information. The Prime Minister said the entire process takes about 15 to 20 minutes. No document needs to be uploaded for this. After submitting the information, people will receive a special ID, which can be shared with the census enumerator when they pay a visit. After the information is verified, it becomes part of the census record. Prime Minister Modi informed that so far, more than 2 crore 60 lakh people have already entered their details on the census portal via mobile, completing the self-enumeration. He said accurate information about citizens and their families helps create a precise picture of the country’s future. The Prime Minister said today marks the 100th birth anniversary of the revered late Ashok Singhal, who was the former International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. He called him a great personality who dedicated his entire life to culture, society, and the nation. Born on 27th September, 1926, in Agra, Ashok Singhal led a life as an ascetic even though living amidst society. Prime Minister Modi said the very direction and energy he imparted to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement veritably resulted in the magnificent temple in Ayodhya today. Alongside the Ram Mandir movement, Ashok Singhal also waged a major battle against social discrimination and inequality. Mr Modi offered his tributes on the occasion of his birth centenary. national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 79 Defence Minister Rajnath Singh says India is building capabilities, keeping in mind the nature of...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today said that India is building capabilities keeping in mind the nature of warfare over the next 10, 20 and 25 years, as it moves towards creating a self-reliant and future-orientated defence ecosystem. He made these remarks while speaking at an event organised by a media house in New Delhi. Mr Singh emphasised that the country should not merely focus on importing technology but should strive to define and develop defence technologies. The Minister said that in the future, the security domain and the battlefield will be technology-driven, and countries that lead in technology will have an advantage on the battlefield. He said this is why India is focusing on making its defence strategy future-ready, with the emphasis not only on developing weapons for today but also on preparing for future challenges. Mr Singh stressed that modern warfare is no longer limited to armed forces or weapons but has become multi-sectoral. Highlighting the growth of the defence sector, he said that over the past 12 years, the country’s defence capabilities have increased significantly, along with a major change in its approach towards strengthening national security. The Minister said that the government has also substantially increased capital allocation in the defence budget. He highlighted that nearly 75 percent of the capital acquisition budget of one lakh 39 thousand crore rupees has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry. Mr Singh said that to promote self-reliance in defence, the armed forces have issued five Positive Indigenisation Lists, covering a total of 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms. Mr Singh iterated that India believes in peace and does not want war. He said India neither wants to occupy the territory of any country nor intimidate any country. He emphasised that there is a difference between peace and weakness. He said India wants peace but will not compromise on its security.

national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, the first One Day International of the 3-match series between India and West Indies will be played today at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. The match will start at 2 PM IST. Both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to India’s ODI lineup after a two-month break from this format. Shubman Gill will lead Team India for this ODI series, while Shai Hope captains the West Indies. Akashvani correspondent reports the enthusiasm among cricket fans, which surged from the opening of ticket sales, has reached its peak with the arrival of both teams in Thiruvananthapuram. Cricket fans in the city are hoping to see India make a strong start in the opening match of the three-match ODI series. Tight security arrangements have been put in place at Thiruvananthapuram in connection with the India-West Indies match. Smithy M Palluruthy, Akashavani News, Thiruvananthapuram.” The second ODI will be played in Guwahati on September 30, followed by the third One Day International in New Chandigarh on October 3. The ODI series will be followed by five T20 internationals. Shreyas Iyer will lead the team in the T20I series. The T20 international series will begin in Lucknow on October 6, followed by the second T20I in Ranchi on October 9, the third in Indore on October 11, the fourth in Hyderabad on October 14, and the fifth in Bengaluru on October 17.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s first world-class geological museum to be developed in Madhya Pradesh 1 hour ago 33
national_raw_news.content: A world-class geological museum, the first of its kind in the country will be developed at the famous Bhedaghat-Lamhetaghat area in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. The Central Government has approved a project worth 87 crore rupees for this. The project will be developed on around 12 hectares of land under the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme. A geological museum and interpretation centre will be built under the project. It will have six galleries and more than 130 exhibits. Other attractions will include 3D models, interactive touch tables, digital panels, an immersive theatre, Titanosaur Square, dinosaur park, fossil garden, geological maze, rock garden, tree-top walkway, glass floor, nature walks and viewing decks. The museum will explain the origin of the Earth and the geological history of the Narmada Valley and Madhya Pradesh, going back millions of years, in a simple and interesting way. The project will focus on protecting the natural surroundings and existing trees. The aim is to keep 90 per cent or more of the area green. Restaurants, food courts, shops selling local products and an eco-resort will also be developed. The project is targeted for completion by February 2028, within 18 months. The Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board will implement the project.

national_raw_news.title: Flood situation worsens in Odisha following continuous heavy rainfall 4 hours ago 105
national_raw_news.content: The flood situation is worsening in several parts of Odisha following heavy rainfall over the past few days, with rivers swelling and low-lying areas inundated. The Jalaka is flowing above the danger level, while the Subarnarekha is rising rapidly, raising concern in northern Odisha. In the Mahanadi basin, heavy rainfall in the upper catchments of Chhattisgarh has increased inflows into Hirakud reservoir, prompting release of excess water through its gates. Akashvani correspondent reports that rainfall continues in several parts of Odisha, aggravating the flood situation in the state. The Jalaka river is flowing above the danger level at Mathani in Balasore district, while the Subarnarekha is also rising and remains close to the danger mark at Rajghat. Several low-lying areas have been inundated. In the Mahanadi basin, heavy rainfall in the upper catchments of Chhattisgarh has led to increased inflow into the Hirakud reservoir. Twenty-two gates of Hirakud Dam are currently open for release of excess water. People living in low-lying areas along the Mahanadi and its tributaries have been advised to remain alert. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast further heavy to very heavy rainfall at some places in Odisha, and authorities are closely monitoring the flood situation.

national_raw_news.title: Rajasthan's Art, Faith, Royalty and Sporting Legacy on Display at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Culture Rajasthan’s Art, Faith, Royalty and Sporting Legacy on Display at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 The collection brings together folk deities, traditional art, textiles, heritage sites and sporting memorabilia, offering a glimpse into Rajasthan’s diverse traditions Posted On: 27 SEP 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi Rajasthan’s rich tapestry of art, devotion, craftsmanship and tradition comes alive in a diverse collection of mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026. The collection brings together 37 artefacts representing the state’s folk deities, traditional paintings, textiles, architectural heritage and sporting achievements. Among the prominent pieces is a handcrafted Ambabari elephant with Howdah, carved from wood and decorated with traditional patterns. Another handcrafted wooden elephant procession set depicts a royal howdah accompanied by ceremonial attendants. The collection highlights a silver memento of Veer Tejaji Maharaj depicts the revered folk deity mounted on a horse, while another silver-plated statue portrays him riding his horse with his characteristic spear and snake motif. The collection includes Pichwai paintings of Shrinathji from Nathdwara, a Phad painting depicting Lakshmi and Narayan and a Pattachitra-style artwork portraying Krishna Raas Leela. These works showcase different forms of devotional storytelling and artistic expression represented in the catalogue. The cultural diversity of the collection extends to Ajmer Sharif Dargah, represented through both a hand-painted artwork and a framed depiction of the shrine. The catalogue describes the painting as capturing the architectural character of the Dargah and its tradition of welcoming devotees from different faiths. A decorated turban featuring a stone and feather brooch, a yellow pagdi with multicoloured motifs, and several angavastras featuring gota borders showcase the region’s textile and ornamental traditions. The collection further features representations of several revered sites and deities, including Kaila Mata of Karauli, Sundha Mata, Khema Baba of Baytu, Brahma Temple in Pushkar and Shri Kalyan Raiji Maharaj. A painting of Mangarh Dham in Banswara also forms part of the collection. Alongside these cultural and sporting artefacts are historical and contemporary memorabilia, including framed newspaper editions related to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha and a decorative plate artwork issued by BJP Rajasthan. Together, the 37 mementos present a varied portrait of Rajasthan through its folk traditions, devotional art, painting, textiles, historical heritage, architecture and contemporary achievements, bringing several facets of the state’s cultural identity into the PM Mementos e-Auction. The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, live until 2 October 2026, brings together mementos representing Rajasthan’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. national_raw_news.title: ICAR-CIRB organises Swachhata Samvad to promote cleanliness, waste management
national_raw_news.content: ICAR-CIRB organises Swachhata Samvad to promote cleanliness, waste management Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर ICAR-CIRB organises Swachhata Samvad to promote cleanliness, waste management ANI | Updated: Sep 27, 2026 17:01 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 27 (ANI): As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign being organised under the theme “Swachhta Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat,” the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes ( ICAR - CIRB ), Hisar, organised a Swachhata Samvad . According to a press release, the initiative was aimed at promoting cleanliness , awareness and active participation among contractual staff and Young Professionals (YPs), while encouraging a clean and hygienic workplace The activity was organised in accordance with the Day-VIII action plan, which envisages Swachhata Samvad as a platform for dialogue and discussion to enhance participation in cleanliness initiatives and promote awareness about hygiene and sustainable waste management. Around 20 participants took part in the interactive programme. As per the release, instead of a conventional lecture-based approach, the Samvad encouraged participants to openly share their experiences, observations, and suggestions on practical cleanliness -related issues in their homes, workplaces, and surrounding areas. Discussions focused on preventing littering, responsible waste disposal, reduction and proper use of plastic, waste segregation, and adoption of sustainable cleanliness practices. The interaction highlighted that cleanliness is not merely a sanitation activity but a shared social responsibility requiring consistent behavioural changes and Jan Bhagidari. Participants discussed how simple practices such as avoiding littering, reducing unnecessary plastic use, segregating waste and ensuring proper disposal can collectively contribute to cleaner and healthier surroundings, said the release. The programme concluded with a collective commitment by the participants to promote cleanliness , responsible waste management and sustainable habits in their respective surroundings. The initiative reflected the spirit of “Swachhta Mein Sahbhag” by encouraging dialogue, participation and collective responsibility towards a cleaner and healthier society. national_raw_news.title: CBN conducts anti-drug awareness programme for students under Mission Yuva Raksha for ...
national_raw_news.content: CBN conducts anti-drug awareness programme for students under Mission Yuva Raksha for Nasha Mukt Bharat in Madhya Pradesh's Jaora Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर CBN conducts anti-drug awareness programme for students under Mission Yuva Raksha for Nasha Mukt Bharat in Madhya Pradesh's Jaora ANI | Updated: Sep 27, 2026 14:47 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 27 (ANI): The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducted a series of significant anti-drug awareness programmes to raise awareness against illegal trafficking and possession of narcotic drugs under Mission Yuva Raksha during the past weeks. Alongside enforcement, CBN continued its preventive awareness and stakeholder outreach initiatives towards the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat. According to the press release issued by the Ministry of Finance, Mission Yuva Raksha, an awareness programme was organised at GT Polytechnic College, Jaora, to sensitise students about the harmful effects of drug abuse, prevention measures and the role of youth in building a drug-free society. Presentations, awareness videos and quiz activities were organised, followed by an anti-drug pledge by the participants. In follow-up to the MoU between CBN and Brahma Kumaris, an awareness programme was organised at Mandsaur, which was attended by approximately 50 opium cultivators and 40 CBN officers. The participants were sensitised about the harmful effects of drug abuse and their role in making India drug-free. The programme concluded with the Nasha Mukt Bharat anti-drug pledge. CBN also conducted Jan Sunwayi programmes at Neemuch and Mandsaur for the prompt and accessible redressal of grievances of opium cultivators. More than 450 cultivators participated in the two programmes. Their grievances and queries, including issues relating to name corrections, Namantaran and eligibility for the upcoming Settlement Operation 2026-27, were heard diligently and addressed promptly. Cultivators were also advised to remain vigilant against middlemen/intermediaries and to approach CBN directly for clarification and assistance. The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) remains firmly committed to the vision of “Safe Use and Prevent Abuse of Drugs or Medicines” and “Nasha Mukt Bharat” and continues to engage with cultivators for their grievance redressal and preventive awareness initiatives against the illegal trafficking, diversion and abuse of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The sustained enforcement operations, coupled with awareness programmes and direct engagement with opium cultivators and youth, reflect CBN’s continued commitment to disrupting illicit drug supply networks, preventing drug abuse and contributing towards a healthier and drug-free society.
